documents.title: Academic Integrity Policy
documents.stance_why: The policy says "Only authorized use of artificial intelligence tools is permitted" and lists "unauthorized use of artificial intelligence tools" as dishonesty, so AI is banned unless authorized. Faculty decide what is authorized and must give "direction on the use of generative artificial intelligence tools, if permitted", but the document itself sets the restrictive default, so restrict rather than delegates.
documents.summary: The university catalog's academic integrity policy treats unauthorized use of AI tools to generate ideas, images, code or text as academic dishonesty. It requires faculty to give AI direction in syllabi and tells unsure students to consult the syllabus or instructor. AI appears in only a few sentences; the sanction ladder is general.

units.why: The sentence frames integrity as shared: "the duty of every community member". It is a general principle, not an AI rule, so it is an informs unit under the institution-wide framework type.
units.anchor: academic integrity as the duty of every community member
units.fit_note: Not AI-specific; it sets the integrity principle under which the AI rules sit.

units.why: The policy says citation procedures differ by circumstance, "including work generated by artificial intelligence tools". It states a fact about AI citation varying, so it informs; P24 is nearest because it concerns citing AI, but it does not itself require disclosure.
units.anchor: including work generated by artificial intelligence tools
units.fit_note: Only acknowledges that AI citation procedures vary by circumstance; it does not require disclosure.

units.why: Faculty "are required to inform students" in syllabi, including "direction on the use of generative artificial intelligence tools". This obliges instructors to state AI expectations in the syllabus, so P09 with instructor as actor.
units.anchor: faculty members are required to inform students of the academic integrity policy

units.why: The same sentence gives AI direction "if permitted for use within the course", so whether AI is allowed is decided course by course. P04 fits better than P09 because this is about who decides, not about stating it.
units.anchor: generative artificial intelligence tools, if permitted for use within the course

units.why: "Students are responsible for understanding the University's policy on academic integrity" puts the duty to know the rules on students. It is not AI-specific; P78 fits as responsibility to know the rules that apply.
units.anchor: Students are responsible for understanding the University's policy on academic integrity.
units.fit_note: Names the university integrity policy rather than each course's AI rules.

units.why: "Only authorized use of artificial intelligence tools is permitted" sets the fallback: what is not authorized is not allowed. That is a default restriction, so P06 (what applies absent permission) rather than P01, because authorization can come from the instructor.
units.anchor: Only authorized use of artificial intelligence tools is permitted.

units.why: Students "unsure about acceptable use of any source, including generative artificial intelligence tools" should "consult the syllabus for a course or speak with the instructor". This tells students to check and ask, so P10; the check-the-syllabus part overlaps P78 but the ask-the-instructor part is the core.
units.anchor: should consult the syllabus for a course or speak with the instructor.

units.why: The list of academic dishonesty includes "unauthorized use of artificial intelligence tools to generate ideas, images, art/design, audio, video, code, or text". It classifies unauthorized AI use as dishonesty, so P36; it also bars generation, but the misconduct classification is the point of the list.
units.anchor: unauthorized use of artificial intelligence tools to generate ideas, images, art/design, audio, video, code

units.why: The outcomes list (warning, probation, suspension, dismissal) is the sanction ladder that applies to AI dishonesty too, so P37.
units.anchor: Academic Integrity Warning, Academic Integrity Probation, Academic Integrity Suspension, and Academic Integrity Dismissal.
units.fit_note: General integrity sanctions, not AI-specific.

units.why: Warning is "issued upon most first minor offenses" and later acts "will result in more severe penalties". A stated first-offense sanction with escalation, so P37.
units.anchor: Academic Integrity Warning status is issued upon most first minor offenses
units.fit_note: General integrity sanction, not AI-specific.

units.why: Students "may be required to participate in a Plagiarism workshop" after a warning. A remedial, educational response rather than only punishment, so P68.
units.anchor: may be required to participate in a Plagiarism workshop offered through the University Learning Center.
units.fit_note: Workshop is for plagiarism generally; AI is not mentioned.

units.why: Probation is "normally issued for serious first offenses", described as premeditated. A stated penalty tier, so P37.
units.anchor: Academic Integrity Probation status is normally issued for serious first offenses
units.fit_note: General integrity sanction, not AI-specific.

units.why: "Academic Integrity Suspension is issued for all egregious infractions" such as repeated dishonesty. A stated penalty tier for repeat offenses, so P37.
units.anchor: Academic Integrity Suspension is issued for all egregious infractions.
units.fit_note: General integrity sanction, not AI-specific.

units.why: Dismissal is for "egregious acts of academic dishonesty related to a major culminating work" such as a thesis. The top penalty tier, so P37.
units.anchor: Academic Integrity Dismissal is issued for all egregious acts of academic dishonesty
units.fit_note: General integrity sanction, not AI-specific.

units.why: The policy points to "Adjudication Procedures" including "a student's right to appeal". Students have a route to contest findings, so P64.
units.anchor: including a student's right to appeal.
units.fit_note: Appeal right applies to all integrity cases; AI is not mentioned.

documents.unit: Guide to Teaching and Learning (Provost's Office / Faculty Center)
documents.title: AI Sample Syllabus Statements
documents.stance_why: The page offers templates and says "Please feel free to adapt suggested language below", with statements running from "explicitly prohibited unless otherwise noted" to "totally unrestricted" use and "encouraged". It sets no single rule and hands the decision to each instructor, so delegates, with the sample statements listed as tiers.
tiers: Generic statement allowing AI with documentation of use
Generic statement prohibiting AI unless the instructor notes otherwise
Course samples in text-based tools: require consult-first, citation or appendix, brainstorming only, expected or required AI use, writing prohibited
Course samples in image-based tools: limited uses with citation, unrestricted use with acknowledgement
documents.summary: The Faculty Center's guide gives instructors general advice (try the tools, talk to students, avoid anthropomorphic language) and sample syllabus statements from prohibition to encouragement, mostly borrowed from other universities. It points to an external repository of statements. One sample is by a New School instructor.

units.why: Faculty "are encouraged to play around with different tools and see what they can - and cannot - do" before deciding. This is support for instructors learning AI before setting policy, so P63.
units.anchor: faculty are encouraged to play around with different tools

units.why: "Please feel free to adapt suggested language below as appropriate to your classes" offers templates instructors choose and change, so each instructor sets the rule: P04.
units.anchor: Please feel free to adapt suggested language below as appropriate to your classes.

units.why: Faculty should "practice transparent teaching" and "Have the conversation with your students" about how AI can support or undermine learning. Explaining and discussing the rules with students is P66.
units.anchor: Have the conversation with your students about how the use of these tools

units.why: If AI is not allowed, faculty should "ask students to consider the skills they may develop during the assignment and why the use of technology would impede that development". This is explaining the reasons behind a rule, so P66.
units.anchor: ask students to consider the skills they may develop during the assignment

units.why: If AI is allowed, faculty "are encouraged to ask or require students to document how they used the tools and what they learned". Documenting use and reflecting is P26.
units.anchor: ask or require students to document how they used the tools and what they learned

units.why: Faculty should "be mindful of using anthropomorphizing language like saying the tool 'created' an image". Careful wording of AI talk is named in P66.
units.anchor: be mindful of using anthropomorphizing language

units.why: The generic allowing statement says "I do not prohibit using any of these tools", so AI is allowed by default with conditions: P02.
units.anchor: I do not prohibit using any of these tools

units.why: "You may not submit materials generated with any AI tool as your own" bars submitting AI output as one's own even where use is allowed: P19.
units.anchor: you may not submit materials generated with any AI tool as your own

units.why: Students who use tools "must document what tools you used, how you used them, what you learned" in a "narrative description or journal entries". A reflection and documentation duty, so P26.
units.anchor: you must document what tools you used, how you used them

units.why: "Please also submit all prompts you used and any interim steps using AI along with the assignment" requires prompts and steps, a transcript-type submission: P26 (P25 would fit only the prompt part).
units.anchor: submit all prompts you used and any interim steps using AI along with the assignment

units.why: "there will be times when we will intentionally use them to learn their value and their limitations" says the course will build AI use into some work, so P79.
units.anchor: we will intentionally use them to learn their value and their limitations

units.why: "We can't always tell when they've been used" admits that AI use cannot be fully verified, so P82; the rationale for transparency.
units.anchor: We can't always tell when they've been used

units.why: The generic prohibiting statement: use of tools "is explicitly prohibited unless otherwise noted by the instructor". A default ban with instructor exceptions, so P01 (the exception clause has the P06 shape, but the ban itself is the main content).
units.anchor: is explicitly prohibited unless otherwise noted by the instructor.

units.why: "using these tools without proper citation constitutes plagiarism" classes uncited use as plagiarism: P36.
units.anchor: using these tools without proper citation constitutes plagiarism.

units.why: The statement warns that "the information derived from these tools is often inaccurate or incomplete", a verification point: P31.
units.anchor: the information derived from these tools is often inaccurate or incomplete.

units.why: "It is imperative that all work submitted be your own" requires submitted work to be the student's: P29.
units.anchor: It is imperative that all work submitted be your own.

units.why: "may receive a zero and / or be reported for academic misconduct" states penalties in advance: P37.
units.anchor: may receive a zero and / or be reported for academic misconduct.

units.why: In the Composition statement, "Development as a writer requires personal investment and practice" explains that practice builds skill, so P41.
units.anchor: Development as a writer requires personal investment and practice.

units.why: "It is important to consult your instructor BEFORE using them in an assignment" tells students to ask first: P10.
units.anchor: It is important to consult your instructor BEFORE using them in an assignment.

units.why: "cite them in your Works Cited page" requires citing AI tools used, so P24.
units.anchor: cite them in your Works Cited page and be prepared to argue a rationale
units.fit_note: Also says students must be ready to argue why the use was appropriate, which P24 does not capture.

units.why: "over reliance on technology can impede the growth of your writing skills" gives the reason AI is limited: reliance undermines skill-building, P41.
units.anchor: over reliance on technology can impede the growth of your writing skills

units.why: The First Year Seminar statement says "It is fine to get research assistance from AI as long as you put both your prompt and the resulting text as an appendix". Research help is allowed with prompt and output attached; P26 as the condition (P12 does not capture the appendix duty).
units.anchor: It is fine to get research assistance from AI as long as you put
units.fit_note: Also permits AI as research assistance; the type captures only the prompt and output appendix.

units.why: "if you use an AI bot's exact words, enclose them in quotes and put the citation in parentheses" treats AI "just as with any other source", so P45.
units.anchor: if you use an AI bot's exact words, enclose them in quotes

units.why: "You are expected to compose the sentences in your written assignments yourself" bars having AI write the submitted text: P19.
units.anchor: You are expected to compose the sentences in your written assignments yourself

units.why: "all existing AI apps 'hallucinate' and supply false information; don't rely on AI for accurate information, but always fact-check" requires verifying output: P31.
units.anchor: always fact-check

units.why: "You may use AI programs e.g. ChatGPT to help generate ideas and brainstorm" permits brainstorming: P15.
units.anchor: You may use AI programs e.g. ChatGPT to help generate ideas and brainstorm.

units.why: "use may also stifle your own independent thinking and creativity" warns AI can displace the student's own thinking: P32.
units.anchor: use may also stifle your own independent thinking and creativity.
units.fit_note: Framed as a warning rather than a requirement that the student stay the primary thinker.

units.why: "You may not submit any work generated by an AI program as your own" is the ban on submitting AI output: P19.
units.anchor: You may not submit any work generated by an AI program as your own.

units.why: "it should be cited like any other reference material" treats AI like another source under citation rules: P45.
units.anchor: it should be cited like any other reference material

units.why: "Any plagiarism or other form of cheating will be dealt with severely" says misuse is handled as misconduct: P36.
units.anchor: Any plagiarism or other form of cheating will be dealt with severely
units.fit_note: Refers to Penn policies, copied from the source course; AI is implied, not named.

units.why: "please write a note to clarify where in your process you used AI and which platform(s) you used" requires a disclosure note: P24.
units.anchor: write a note to clarify where in your process you used AI

units.why: "We will discuss this more throughout the semester in class" commits to ongoing class discussion of AI use: P66.
units.anchor: We will discuss this more throughout the semester in class

units.why: "what the AI writing tools generate is often inaccurate" warns of errors: P31.
units.anchor: what the AI writing tools generate is often inaccurate

units.why: "I expect you to use AI (ChatGPT and image generation tools, at a minimum), in this class" with "some assignments will require it" builds AI into the course: P79.
units.anchor: I expect you to use AI (ChatGPT and image generation tools, at a minimum)

units.why: "Learning to use AI is an emerging skill, and I provide tutorials in Canvas" teaches AI use as a skill: P44.
units.anchor: Learning to use AI is an emerging skill, and I provide tutorials in Canvas

units.why: "I am happy to meet and help with these tools during office hours or after class" points students to human help: P72.
units.anchor: I am happy to meet and help with these tools during office hours
units.fit_note: Instructor offers help using the AI tools themselves.

units.why: "If you provide minimum effort prompts, you will get low quality results. You will need to refine your prompts" gives prompting advice: P93.
units.anchor: You will need to refine your prompts in order to get good outcomes.

units.why: "Don't trust anything it says" tells students to check output: P31.
units.anchor: Don't trust anything it says.

units.why: "You will be responsible for any errors or omissions provided by the tool" makes students answerable for AI output: P29.
units.anchor: You will be responsible for any errors or omissions provided by the tool.

units.why: "Please include a paragraph at the end of any assignment that uses AI explaining what you used the AI for and what prompts you used" is a disclosure statement with prompts: P24.
units.anchor: include a paragraph at the end of any assignment that uses AI explaining what
units.fit_note: Also asks for the prompts used, which is more specific than P24.

units.why: "Failure to do so is in violation of the academic honesty policies" makes non-disclosure the violation: P28.
units.anchor: Failure to do so is in violation of the academic honesty policies.

units.why: "Be thoughtful about when this tool is useful. Don't use it if it isn't appropriate" asks students to judge fit; P32 is nearest (students stay the decision-maker).
units.anchor: Don't use it if it isn't appropriate for the case or circumstance.
units.fit_note: Asks for judgment about when AI is appropriate; no criteria given.

units.why: "all writing assignments should be prepared by the student" because "writing, analytical, and critical thinking skills are part of the learning outcomes". Ties the rule to learning objectives: P83.
units.anchor: writing, analytical, and critical thinking skills are part of the learning outcomes of this course

units.why: "all writing assignments should be prepared by the student" bars AI-prepared writing: P19.
units.anchor: all writing assignments should be prepared by the student.

units.why: "Developing strong competencies in this area will prepare you for a competitive workplace" gives careers as the reason to build skills without AI: P94.
units.anchor: Developing strong competencies in this area will prepare you for a competitive workplace.

units.why: "AI-generated submissions are not permitted and will be treated as plagiarism" is a ban plus misconduct classification. I chose P36 because the classification is the new content; the ban is covered by the writing rule above.
units.anchor: AI-generated submissions are not permitted and will be treated as plagiarism.

units.why: "AI generators make mistakes. Assume the output is incorrect unless you check the claims with reliable sources" requires verification: P31.
units.anchor: Assume the output is incorrect unless you check the claims with reliable sources.

units.why: "Their output may reflect bias because the data they are trained on may reflect bias" names bias as a concern: P53.
units.anchor: Their output may reflect bias because the data they are trained on may reflect bias

units.why: "These tools use existing sources without citation. Therefore using their outputs puts you at risk of plagiarism" warns that AI output can carry uncited sources, which no listed type captures.
units.anchor: These tools use existing sources without citation.
units.uncovered_note: AI tools reuse existing sources without citation, so using their output risks plagiarism.

units.why: "Each ChatGPT search uses non-trivial amounts of electricity and water" names an environmental cost: P53.
units.anchor: Each ChatGPT search uses non-trivial amounts of electricity and water.

units.why: Students "are welcome to use AI generators to brainstorm and refine ideas, find sources (that you subsequently read)" permits brainstorming and exploring: P15.
units.anchor: you are welcome to use AI generators to brainstorm and refine ideas, find sources
units.fit_note: The same sentence also lists finding sources that students must read themselves.

units.why: "draft outlines, check grammar, refine wording, and format bibliographies" permits editing and writing support: P91.
units.anchor: draft outlines, check grammar, refine wording, and format bibliographies.

units.why: "Beyond bibliographic references, you are not allowed to copy and paste material generated by AI" is a no-copy-paste rule: P23.
units.anchor: you are not allowed to copy and paste material generated by AI

units.why: "add a note indicating which AI tool you used and how you used it, including the prompt(s) you used and the date(s)" requires tool, prompt and date: P25.
units.anchor: add a note indicating which AI tool you used and how you used it

units.why: "I may sometimes incorporate the use of generative artificial intelligence (AI) tools like ChatGPT into your lessons and assignments" says AI will be used in some assigned work: P79.
units.anchor: I may sometimes incorporate the use of generative artificial intelligence (AI) tools
units.fit_note: Instructor says AI use will sometimes be assigned; not a standing requirement.

units.why: "in instances where you are not specifically told to use AI, I ask you to ... write without using AI" sets the fallback when AI is not assigned: P06.
units.anchor: in instances where you are not specifically told to use AI

units.why: "You MAY use AI in the initial stages of research, idea generation, and drafting" permits early-stage use: P15.
units.anchor: You MAY use AI in the initial stages of research, idea generation, and drafting.
units.fit_note: Also covers research and drafting stages, not only brainstorming.

units.why: "You MAY use AI for language translation" permits a prose-support use: P18.
units.anchor: You MAY use AI for language translation.
units.fit_note: Permission itself; P18 is about separate prose rules.

units.why: "you MAY NOT not rely on AI output for significant portions of your final project form" caps reliance on AI in the final form: P19.
units.anchor: you MAY NOT not rely on AI output for significant portions of your final project
units.fit_note: Bans reliance for significant portions unless essential to the project concept, a partial bar.

units.why: "you must properly cite and disclose this use" at any stage requires disclosure: P24.
units.anchor: you must properly cite and disclose this use.

units.why: "details on the specific tool and version used, as well as the nature of your usage" requires tool, version and kind of use: P25.
units.anchor: details on the specific tool and version used, as well as the nature

units.why: "Citation should reference both the platform and any creator ('style of') names or references" adds a rule for image tools: P25.
units.anchor: Citation should reference both the platform and any creator
units.fit_note: Also asks for 'style of' artist names, specific to image generation.

units.why: "you are welcome to use foundation models ... in a totally unrestricted fashion, for any purpose, at no penalty" is open permission: P02.
units.anchor: you are welcome to use foundation models

units.why: "You will be responsible for any inaccurate, biased, offensive, or otherwise unethical content you submit" makes the student answerable regardless of source: P29.
units.anchor: You will be responsible for any inaccurate, biased, offensive, or otherwise unethical content you submit

units.why: "its contribution must be acknowledged in the hand-in; you will be penalized for using a foundation model without acknowledgement" makes non-disclosure the penalized act: P28.
units.anchor: you will be penalized for using a foundation model without acknowledgement.
units.fit_note: Also requires acknowledgement itself.

units.why: "the use of foundation models is encouraged, as it may make it possible for you to submit assignments with higher quality, in less time" names a benefit: P87 (P02 covers the permission, coded above).
units.anchor: the use of foundation models is encouraged, as it may make it possible

units.why: "all large language models still have a tendency to make up incorrect facts and fake citations" warns of errors: P31.
units.anchor: large language models still have a tendency to make up incorrect facts and fake citations

units.why: "The university's policy on plagiarism still applies" to uncited use of work by other humans, so existing university policy continues to govern: P77.
units.anchor: The university's policy on plagiarism still applies
units.fit_note: Applies to work by other human beings, not to AI use.

units.why: The page directs faculty to "a large repository of statements for individual courses", a resource for instructors: P63.
units.anchor: A link to a large repository of statements for individual courses
units.fit_note: Resource pointer only.

notes: Coder B. Sample statements on the Guide page are mostly from other universities (Tennessee State, Ohio, Penn, USC, etc.) and one from The New School (Design and Technology); coded as the page's content. Integrity sanction tiers are general, not AI-specific, and noted as such.
